hook.text: Not all tornadoes come from supercells—some spin up from boundaries and collisions without any parent storm.

buildup.text: Landspouts form when surface wind convergence along a boundary creates rotation that gets stretched vertically.

discovery.text: Waterspouts are the oceanic cousins—forming over warm water, typically weak and short-lived.

twist.text: Gustnadoes spin up along gust fronts—they look like tornadoes but aren't connected to a cloud base.

climax.text: These non-supercell tornadoes are weaker but also harder to warn for—they form with little radar signature.

punchline.text: No supercell needed—sometimes the ground does the spinning.

quiz.question: What is a landspout?
options: A tornado formed from surface convergence without a mesocyclone
A dust devil in a storm
